units.intent: Wraps a single sqlite3 handle with Bedrock's replicated-transaction model: journal-table bookkeeping, begin/read/write/prepare/commit/rollback, a cross-handle commit-order mutex, query result caching, conflict-location reporting, and authorizer/rewrite/whitelist hooks used by the sync layer and commands.

objects.name: SQLite
objects.role: owns the sqlite3* handle and drives the transaction/journal/replication lifecycle

objects.name: SQLite::Parameter
objects.role: re-export of SQliteParameter for bound-parameter query calls

objects.name: SQLite::timeout_error
objects.role: thrown when a query exceeds its configured timeout

objects.name: SQLite::constraint_error
objects.role: marks a SQLITE_CONSTRAINT failure as a benign replication-ordering race rather than a real error

objects.name: SQLite::TRANSACTION_TYPE
objects.role: SHARED vs EXCLUSIVE transaction locking mode

objects.name: SQLite::SharedData
objects.role: state shared by every SQLite handle on the same file: commit count/mutex, checkpoint state, prepared/committed transaction queues

objects.name: SQLite::COMMIT_DISABLED
objects.role: sentinel result code returned by commit() when commits are administratively disabled

objects.name: DBINFO
objects.role: logs an SINFO line prefixed with the DB filename

objects.name: SharedDataLookupMapType
objects.role: static process-lifetime filename -> SharedData* registry

misfits.why: query-rewriting exists, per its own comment, "to support mocked requests and load testing" - a test/mock-only feature wired directly into the production replicated-DB class
noop-update mode is documented as existing only for `mockRequest`-enabled command testing, but lives as first-class state on the core DB class

core sqlitecluster engine depends on plugins/Compression, a Bedrock command plugin, to compress journal entries and register SQLite UDFs - an inverted layering dependency for a library that otherwise only depends on libstuff
misfits.suggested_home: a libstuff/sqlitecluster-level compression helper that plugins/Compression itself builds on, instead of the reverse

misfits.item: Commented-out HC-Tree slow-commit diagnostic block inside SQLite::commit()
misfits.why: ~15 lines of disabled debug-logging code left in place rather than removed or gated behind a runtime flag
per its own comment this exists specifically to support the BlockWrites command - a single command's requirement implemented as a generic-looking member of the cross-handle SharedData structure

name_fit.note: SQLite.h/.cpp is exactly the DB-engine wrapper class for sqlitecluster.

location_fit.note: Right directory for the class itself; docked for reaching into plugins/Compression from a core library (see misfits).

naming_quality.note: Consistent `_`-prefixed privates overall, but getLastConflictIdentifier() actually returns _lastConflictPage while a separate thread_local _conflictIdentifier covers the HC-Tree case - two conflict-identity concepts share one public getter name.

units.intent: Escalates a BedrockCommand from this node to another node in the cluster (leader, a named peer, or all peers) over a pooled TCP socket and fills in the command's response.

objects.name: SQLiteClusterMessenger
objects.role: opens/reuses a socket to a peer, sends a serialized command, and reads back its response

objects.name: SQLiteClusterMessenger::WaitForReadyResult
objects.role: outcome of waiting for a socket to become ready (timeout, disconnect, abort, etc.)

name_fit.note: clearly a messenger between nodes, sits correctly with SQLiteNode/SQLitePeer.

naming_quality.note: two overloaded runOnPeer methods (bool vs. peer-name) have different retry semantics but the same name.

units.intent: Base representation of a command as it moves through the cluster: wire-format request/response, a cross-node id, completion flag, and escalation timing; BedrockCommand builds on top of it.

objects.name: SQLiteCommand
objects.role: holds request/response/id/timing for a command; move-only via a private backing field for the const `request` reference

objects.name: SQLiteCommand::preprocessRequest
objects.role: assigns a requestID and warns on deprecated commandExecuteTime, run before `request` is bound

misfits.why: deprecation-specific handling of one legacy wire field living inside an otherwise generic request-preprocessing helper

location_fit.note: correctly the base type alongside the rest of sqlitecluster.

naming_quality.note: private backing field is named `privateRequest` instead of the repo's usual `_` prefix (e.g. `_request`), inconsistent with the rest of the codebase's own convention.

units.intent: Wraps commit/rollback of a SQLite database with the cluster-aware checks needed to do so safely: only commit while still leader, and run an optional plugin-notification hook during prepare.

objects.name: SQLiteCore
objects.role: commits or rolls back a transaction on a wrapped SQLite&, refusing to commit if the node is no longer leading

name_fit.note: "Core" is a bit generic but the content (commit/rollback gating) is coherent and singular.

naming_quality.note: notificationHandler's function-pointer parameter is named `_db`, echoing the class's own `_db` member despite being an unrelated parameter.

units.intent: A distributed, leader/follower, failover SQLite cluster node: maintains peer connections, drives the cluster's leader-election state machine (SEARCHING through LEADING/FOLLOWING), and replicates committed transactions between leader and followers.

objects.name: SQLiteNodeState
objects.role: the states a node cycles through in the cluster state machine

objects.name: SQLiteNode
objects.role: STCPManager subclass owning the peer list and command port; drives the state machine and replication

objects.name: PDEBUG/PINFO/PHMMM/PWARN
objects.role: logging macros that prefix a log line with "->{peer->name}", used wherever a peer is in scope

objects.name: synchronizeCount
objects.role: numbers each spawned synchronize-response thread for its SInitialize() label

objects.name: SQLiteNode::stateName/stateFromName lookup tables
objects.role: translate between SQLiteNodeState and its string name

misfits.item: #include <plugins/Compression.h> and BedrockPlugin_Compression::decompress calls in SQLiteNode.cpp's _handleBeginTransaction and _recvSynchronize
misfits.why: sqlitecluster/ is a lower-level replication library depending directly on one specific plugin under plugins/, inverting the codebase's normal dependency direction (plugins depend on sqlitecluster, not the reverse); sqlitecluster/SQLite.cpp has the same dependency, so it's an established pattern rather than unique to this file

a global static pointer/flag letting process-wide signal-handling code reach into one specific node instance to kill its sockets; shutdown coordination bolted onto the node class rather than a dedicated signal-handling module
both carry inline comments marking them "Remove" with links to open GitHub issues (208449, 208439) -- acknowledged, unresolved design debt in the node's state tracking

location_fit.note: sqlitecluster/ is exactly right for the cluster-replication node

naming_quality.note: consistent underscore-prefix for private members overall, but `pluginDB` is a private member with no underscore, and `messagesDeqeued` in _processPeerMessages is a typo for "messagesDequeued"

units.intent: Represents one other node in the cluster as seen from this node: its connection socket, replication state, and the synchronization/standup metadata SQLiteNode needs to run consensus.

objects.name: SQLitePeer
objects.role: one peer's connection + replication/consensus state, guarded by an internal mutex

objects.name: SQLitePeer::Response
objects.role: a peer's vote on a standup request (NONE/APPROVE/DENY)

objects.name: SQLitePeer::PeerPostPollStatus
objects.role: result of postPoll: OK, just-connected, socket error, or socket closed

objects.name: operator<<(ostream&, atomic<SQLitePeer::Response>&)
objects.role: streams a Response's name

misfits.why: claims 'see friend class declaration above' but no friend is declared anywhere in this file - a stale/incorrect cross-reference left over from an earlier version

name_fit.note: does exactly what the name says.

naming_quality.note: consistent S-prefix and trailing-underscore constructor params; the stale friend-class comment is a minor documentation defect.

units.intent: Hands out SQLite database handles to worker threads from a bounded pool, creating new handles lazily up to a max and blocking callers when it's exhausted.

objects.name: SQLitePool
objects.role: bounded pool of SQLite handles cloned from one base handle; get/initialize/return an index

objects.name: SQLiteScopedHandle
objects.role: RAII wrapper that returns its pool index to the pool when it goes out of scope

naming_quality.note: consistent with repo convention; getIndex returns a bare size_t rather than a typed token, so any size_t can be passed to returnToPool.

units.intent: Abstract interface a SQLiteNode uses to call back into whatever server embeds it: login notifications, state-change notifications to plugins, and command-port blocking.

objects.name: SQLiteServer
objects.role: pure-virtual interface (onNodeLogin, notifyStateChangeToPlugins, blockCommandPort, unblockCommandPort), extends STCPManager

location_fit.note: the callback contract for SQLiteNode's host server belongs here.

units.intent: Generates a random, table-unique int64 ID for use as a primary key.

objects.name: SQLiteUtils
objects.role: static-only helper; getRandomID picks a random ID and retries until it's not already present in the given table/column

name_fit.note: "Utils" is generic for a single-function class, though the single function itself is coherent.

location_fit.note: SQLite-specific ID generation belongs in sqlitecluster.

naming_quality.note: fine as far as it goes; a one-function Utils class invites unrelated helpers to accrete.
